design: C1 = frozen internal features plus small U-Net
question: Can multiscale spatial context improve the strong feature-informed residual and reduce patch-like corrections without sacrificing boundaries?
reference_scope: R0, frozen_features and unet have complete three-seed results. Historical bundle seed320114 is still running independently; final method selection waits for all experiments.
fixed: original D0 base; no flip/scale preprocessing

additional_controls.C1_zero_features: Same architecture and parameter count, replace internal feature tensor with zeros. This removes observable information; projection weights receive no input-dependent gradient, so it is not equal effective functional capacity.
additional_controls.C1_no_rgb: Remove RGB channels; retain original predicted log depth and frozen features. Motivated by depth-only screening and possible texture leakage. Single-seed diagnostic initially.

bounded_revision: At most one revised combination may be promoted. If removing RGB improves AbsRel and does not lower boundary F1 vs matched-seed C1, it may receive seeds320113/320114 as the single allowed revision. Otherwise retain this as a negative/ambiguous ablation and do not open an unbounded architecture/input search. No automatic edge/ensemble expansion.
selection_rule: Final selection uses completed development evidence, primary mean AbsRel with scene/seed uncertainty, boundary tradeoffs and cost; no new test results. One-seed ablation results are labeled exploratory.
